page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an AWS Graviton2 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture, operating at a fixed clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It provisions 8 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual CPU thread mapping, omitting hyper-threading. The CPU subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, backed by standard hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions.

System memory consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. A key defining hardware attribute is the included high-capacity direct-attached local storage, which provides 3750 GB across local NVMe SSD media. Network connectivity features a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and the instance is optimized for Amazon Elastic Block Store traffic. Accelerated computing hardware is not present, with zero dedicated GPUs attached.

Benchmark results show balanced throughput in multi-threaded computational workloads, registering 12,131.82 on stress-ng multi-core and 5,430.0 on Geekbench multi-core, both placing within average performance tiers. In-memory operations show reliable execution, achieving 9.97 million Redis SET operations per second and 5,226.37 in PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-thread compute capabilities remain modest, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0, a PassMark CPU score of 5,240.63, and bottom-tier results in compression algorithms such as single-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU encryption.

The im4gn.2xlarge offers favorable resource density for I/O-intensive services requiring localized storage footprints alongside ARM power efficiency. With 3.75 TB of fast NVMe storage bound to 8 dedicated ARM cores, it avoids the latency overhead and external pricing tiers of remote network-attached disks. The instance is best matched for distributed data stores, transactional and NoSQL databases, log analysis engines, caching platforms, and data processing pipelines that rely heavily on fast local disk access rather than peak single-core scalar throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance engineered around the 64-bit ARM architecture using the AWS Nitro system. Powered by an AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio, complemented by 12 Gbps baseline networking and 3750 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. It includes no graphics accelerators. Benchmark metrics place multi-core CPU and transactional data operations within median ranges, evidenced by 9.97 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core scalar and compression benchmarks perform within lower percentiles. The hardware configuration delivers high local NVMe storage density per vCPU, making it optimal for intermediate-scale databases, search nodes, log indexing, and distributed storage systems requiring dense local disk throughput.
